feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 is the only evidence: about 1 line-loss event per run on all tracks, max_error about 0.0626 m (just over the 0.06 m off-track limit), and 19 of 20 oval trials and all s-bend and slalom trials ending off track. That pattern supports the sensor-coverage explanation in your rationale, because the five-sensor span (±0.04 m) loses the tape close to the off-track boundary. I have not measured the seven-sensor row, so the following depends on the next race. If line_loss_events falls to zero or near zero and max_error stays below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, keep the ±0.06 m span and treat sensing as solved. If line_loss_events stays near 1 while the robot still leaves at the same bend, sensing is not the limit and the next change should be to wheel_track, not the sensor row. If steering_oscillation rises well above iteration 0 (about 0.30 on the oval) with no line loss, the outer sensors are probably overdriving the signal, so reduce the outer weights or move the outer sensors inward. Please keep the 0.02 m spacing and 12 mm footprints so the signal stays continuous across the tape.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stays at about 1 per run on s-bend and slalom with max_error near 0.06 m, extend the row to x = ±0.07 m (seven sensors at about 0.0233 m spacing, 0.012 m footprints, y = 0.04) to add coverage margin. Iteration 0 shows the tape is lost at about ±0.058 m with the ±0.04 m row.

If steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 0 oval level of about 0.30 with no line loss, reduce the outer sensor influence by changing the outer sensor x to ±0.05 m with the same seven-sensor count, or leave the geometry and let the Integrator reduce kp. This addresses the edge-gain concern in your question.

If completion is still 0 with progress well short of 1 and no line loss, widen wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.14 m with the sensor row fixed, to isolate turn authority. Iteration 0 showed off-track ends with no line-loss problem on the s-bend, which points to turn limits rather than sensing.
